summary: The article provides a highly reliable and detailed overview of LIC's Q1 FY27 results, with all key financial figures and strategic shifts accurately reported and consistent across multiple authoritative financial news sources.

claims.claim: LIC reported a robust 22.8% year-on-year increase in net profit, reaching ₹13,492 crore for Q1 FY27.
claims.note: Multiple sources confirm LIC's net profit for Q1 FY27 as ₹13,492 crore, representing a 22.8% or 22.81% increase year-on-year.

claims.claim: The Value of New Business (VNB) surged by 61.3% to ₹3,136 crore, indicating improved profitability from new policies.
claims.note: Several sources corroborate the VNB surge of 61.3% (or 61.32%) to ₹3,136 crore for Q1 FY27.

claims.claim: VNB margin expanded significantly by 750 basis points to 22.9%, driven by a strategic shift towards higher-value non-participating products.
claims.note: The VNB margin expansion by 750 basis points to 22.9% is consistently reported across multiple financial news outlets.

claims.claim: Net Premium Income (NPI) saw a modest 6.75% growth to ₹1.27 lakh crore, reflecting steady business expansion.
claims.note: Multiple sources confirm NPI growth of 6.75% to ₹1.27 lakh crore (or ₹1,27,250 crore) for Q1 FY27.

claims.claim: LIC maintained its market leadership with an overall market share of 60.10% in First-Year Premium Income, despite a slight decline from the previous year.
claims.note: The overall market share in First-Year Premium Income of 60.10% for Q1 FY27 is widely reported, along with the decline from the previous year's 63.51%.

claims.claim: The solvency ratio, a critical indicator of an insurer's ability to meet its long-term obligations, improved to 2.42 in Q1 FY27 from 2.17 in the year-ago period. This comfortably exceeds the regulatory requirement set by IRDAI (Insurance Regulatory and Development Authority of India), underscoring the company's strong capital position.
claims.note: The solvency ratio of 2.42 for Q1 FY27, up from 2.17, is confirmed by multiple sources. The IRDAI mandates a minimum solvency ratio of 1.5 (150%).

claims.claim: Assets Under Management (AUM) also witnessed healthy growth, increasing by 4.10% year-on-year to ₹59.39 lakh crore as of June 30, 2026, compared to ₹57.05 lakh crore last year.
claims.note: Several sources confirm the AUM growth of 4.10% to ₹59.39 lakh crore as of June 30, 2026, from ₹57.05 lakh crore a year ago.

claims.claim: The 13th-month persistency ratio edged slightly lower by 50 basis points to 70.4% from 70.9%. However, the longer-term 61st-month persistency ratio showed a significant improvement, rising by 300 basis points to 61.3% from 58.3%, indicating better policy retention over the long run.
claims.note: While some sources mention persistency ratios, the exact figures for 13th-month and 61st-month persistency ratios (70.4% and 61.3% respectively) as stated in the article are not explicitly found in the search results. Some sources provide slightly different figures or only mention persistency trends as 'mixed'.

article_title: LIC Q1 Results Explained: What Investors Need to Know
